extracted.intended_audience: Nonprofit staff, leaders, and advocates at 501(c)(3) organizations preparing public comments on federal rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for nonprofit organizations on preparing and submitting public comments to federal rulemaking processes, including framing, evidence, coordination, and legal compliance considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame comments with organization's mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the organization's mission as the framing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with how the proposed rule relates to your nonprofit's mission and institutional role; explain why the issue matters to your organization rather than speaking only as an individual. Use mission-based framing to establish relevance and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speak from sector expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Speak from sector expertise (e.g., human services, arts, environmental)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize your sector-specific knowledge and programmatic experience. Provide concrete examples from your service area to show subject-matter expertise and the practical implications of the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite empirical data from direct service experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite empirical data from your direct service experience
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include quantitative evidence (service counts, outcomes, metrics) and qualitative evidence from your programs. Where possible, provide sources, dates, and methods for data to bolster the credibility of claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate impacts across the population you serve
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate impacts across the population you serve
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe aggregate numbers and patterns (e.g., total clients affected, geographic distribution) rather than only individual anecdotes to demonstrate wider impact and representativeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame harms and benefits in terms of affected public
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame harm/benefit in terms of the public the rule affects
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the rule will help or harm the public or communities you serve—focus on concrete consequences for access, costs, equity, and outcomes rather than abstract policy arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid partisan framing (comply with 501(c)(3) rules)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use nonpartisan language; do not endorse or oppose political candidates. Ensure advocacy stays within allowable activities for 501(c)(3) organizations and use available lobbying-limit calculators to check compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific about regulatory provisions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference the exact regulatory sections, quoted language, or specific provisions you are addressing. Propose concrete edits or alternatives rather than only making high-level statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with peer organizations and use sign-on letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate with peer organizations through sign-on letters when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sign-on letters to amplify messages and help smaller organizations be heard; coordinate timing, messaging, and logistics with coalition partners and use coalition resources offered by the Council.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sample templates and issue-specific talking points
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Council's sample comment templates and issue-specific talking points
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage customizable templates and talking points to streamline drafting, while adapting them to your mission, data, and local context. Monitor action alerts for major proposed rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand nonprofit-specific legal/advocacy considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonprofits speaking as institutions can endorse/oppose specific rules without 501(h) lobbying limits
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know the distinction between institutional comment activity and lobbying limits (501(h)); use Council resources and lobbying-limit calculators to determine what advocacy activities are permissible for your organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve client confidentiality when aggregating perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonprofit comments should preserve client confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using client stories or data, anonymize personally identifiable information and obtain consent when necessary. Protect beneficiary privacy while describing impacts and experiences.
